title: U.S. House · Alaska At-Large
area: Statewide, Alaska's single at-large congressional district.

context.text: Alaska uses a top-four nonpartisan primary followed by ranked-choice voting in the general election. Incumbent Nicholas Begich (R) won the August 18, 2026 primary with 44.6%, followed by Bill Hill (Nonpartisan) with 32.5%. John Brendan Williams (D), who placed fifth, withdrew from the general election; Jim McDermott (L), who finished eighth, replaced him on the ballot.

candidates.name: Nicholas Begich

summary.text: Nicholas Begich is the Republican incumbent seeking a second term in Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat, first elected in 2024. A Chugiak resident born in Anchorage, he worked at Ford Motor Company before returning to Alaska in 2004 and starting technology and investment businesses, including FarShore Partners and Dashfire. He previously ran for Anchorage City Council (2016) and for this House seat in 2022.

background.text: Born in Anchorage, Alaska, and raised by his maternal grandparents, according to his congressional website; he lives in Chugiak with his wife, Dharna, and their son.
Earned a B.B.A. in entrepreneurship from Baylor University (1999) and an M.B.A. from Indiana University-Bloomington (2002).
According to his congressional website, was recruited by Ford Motor Company, where he worked in technology, finance and product development, before he and his wife returned to Alaska in 2004.
Founded FarShore Partners, a technology development company, and co-founded Dashfire, a startup investment firm; his congressional website also says he has served as a startup coach and mentor.

Completed a fellowship with the Club for Growth and co-chaired the Alaska Republican Party's Finance Committee and Rep. Don Young's 2020 re-election campaign. His congressional website also lists prior work with the Alaska Policy Forum and service as a board director of Matanuska Telecom Association.
Ran for Anchorage City Council (District 2, Seat A) in 2016 and lost to incumbent Amy Demboski, 57.7% to 41.7%.
Ran for Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat in 2022, finishing third in the first round of the ranked-choice count behind Mary Peltola and Sarah Palin; Peltola won.
Won the 2024 general election for the at-large U.S. House seat over Mary Peltola, 51.2% to 48.8% after ranked-choice tabulation, and took office in 2025.
Committee assignments for 2025-2026 include Natural Resources (Vice Chair of the Energy and Mineral Resources subcommittee), Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology.

positions.summary: Co-sponsored H.R. 30, the Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act, and voted for the Laken Riley Act, saying both give law enforcement more tools to detain and remove immigrants in the country illegally who commit crimes.
positions.quote: Securing our borders is both a matter of national security and a matter of protecting those closest to us—family, friends, colleagues, neighbors, and indeed all Americans.

positions.summary: Defended the Trump administration's tariffs on China in a television interview, framing them as a response to China's own trade restrictions and export controls.
positions.quote: What Donald Trump is doing is standing up for America and Americans, and he is putting America First. He is pushing back on China’s own tariffs and export controls against the United States, and I think it opens the opportunity for us to have a broader conversation.

positions.summary: Voted against a three-year extension of ACA health insurance subsidies, saying the underlying law needs structural reform rather than a temporary extension.
positions.quote: The health insurance system created by Democrats under Obamacare has proven completely unaffordable for the American healthcare customer.

record.text: Serves on the House Natural Resources Committee (Vice Chair of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee), the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee in the 119th Congress.

summary.text: Bill Hill is a nonpartisan candidate who finished second in the August 2026 top-four primary. A Dena'ina Athabascan raised in Kokhanok and now living in Naknek, he is a Bristol Bay commercial fisherman and retired educator who served as a teacher and as superintendent of two school districts. He is running on affordability, ending congressional stock trading, and fisheries issues, and has not said which caucus he would join.

background.text: Dena'ina Athabascan; raised in Kokhanok on Lake Iliamna before moving to Naknek in high school, according to KDLG. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes growing up in a small village in rural Alaska, hunting, fishing and raising sled dog teams.
Graduated from the University of Alaska and has lived in Fairbanks and Juneau, according to KDLG.

Worked as a teacher in Naknek and Juneau, as an administrator in the Lake and Peninsula School District, and as superintendent of the Bristol Bay district, and also worked in construction and ran a small business, according to Alaska Public Media.

Served as superintendent of both the Lake and Peninsula School District and the Bristol Bay Borough School District, and was named Alaska Superintendent of the Year in 2023, before retiring from education, according to KDLG.
Describes himself as a lifelong fisherman and a commercial fisherman in Bristol Bay, and has also worked as a school teacher and construction worker.

Announced his candidacy in January 2026 as an independent; says he has always been an unaffiliated voter. A day after launching, his campaign said it had raised $200,000, and Alaska House Speaker Bryce Edgmon endorsed him.
Finished second in the August 18, 2026 primary with 32.5% of the vote.
Lives in Naknek with his wife, Diane, and describes himself as a father of four and grandfather of seven.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of gas, groceries, and healthcare for Alaskans, citing fuel prices as high as $15 a gallon in some rural communities.
A total ban on congressional stock trading and reducing the influence of money in elections.
Opposing trawl bycatch to protect Alaska fisheries, and investing in schools.

positions.summary: Says billionaires and corporations need to pay their share like everyone else, as part of his campaign against what he calls the corrupt D.C. elite.
positions.quote: Billionaires and corporations need to pay their share like the rest of us. And we need to get big money out of our elections.

candidates.name: Eric Hafner

summary.text: Eric Hafner is the Democratic nominee. He previously ran in a 2016 Republican primary in Hawaii and a 2018 Democratic primary in Oregon, and advanced to the 2024 Alaska general election ballot. According to Ballotpedia, he was serving a 20-year federal sentence for threatening elected officials when the Alaska Democratic Party sued in 2024 to remove him from the ballot.

background.text: Described in a 2022 New Jersey Globe report as a Toms River, New Jersey, medical marijuana advocate; the report said he was living outside the U.S. when the conduct at issue in his criminal case occurred (2016-2018).

Lost a Republican primary for Congress in Hawaii in 2016, taking 44% of the vote, and a Democratic primary in Oregon's 3rd District in 2018 (1.4% per Ballotpedia), according to the New Jersey Globe and Ballotpedia.

In his 2018 Ballotpedia survey, listed past work as a diplomatic advisor, criminal defense consultant, union organizer, hotel manager, real estate marketing assistant, medical cannabis policy advisor to Manalapan Township, New Jersey, political consultant and field organizer.

In May 2022, the New Jersey Globe reported that he pleaded guilty in federal court to threatening judges, New Jersey officials and law enforcement and to making false bomb threats; prosecutors said he sought to extort $350,000 from some victims.

At the time of a 2024 Alaska Democratic Party lawsuit seeking to remove him from that year's ballot, Hafner was serving a 20-year federal prison sentence in New York for threatening elected officials, with a scheduled release in 2036.

An Alaska Superior Court judge dismissed the party's 2024 lawsuit, ruling that ranked-choice voting eliminated any claim of harm from his presence on the ballot and that the court could not weigh in on whether he would reside in Alaska by Election Day.
Finished fourth in the August 18, 2026 primary with 3.8% of the vote.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statement of positions could be located; Hafner has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Ballotpedia's coverage of Hafner focuses on the ballot-eligibility litigation rather than a policy platform.

candidates.name: Jim McDermott

summary.text: Jim McDermott is the Libertarian nominee. A 22-year U.S. Air Force veteran and business instructor at the University of Alaska, he previously ran as a Libertarian for this seat in 2012, 2014 and 2016. He finished eighth in the August 2026 primary and joined the general-election ballot after a higher-finishing candidate withdrew.

background.text: Holds a B.S. in occupational education from Wayland Baptist University and an M.S. in business organizational management from the University of La Verne.
Served 22 years in the U.S. Air Force and works as a business instructor for the University of Alaska.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat in 2012, losing to Rep. Don Young.
In 2014, won the Libertarian nomination unopposed and received 7.6% of the vote (21,290 votes) in the general election, finishing third behind Don Young and Forrest Dunbar.
Ran again in 2016 as the Libertarian candidate, again losing to Young.
In 2026, finished in the August primary with 1.2% of the vote and replaced Democrat John Brendan Williams on the general-election ballot after Williams withdrew.

candidates.researchNotes: McDermott has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website content with specific 2026 positions could be located.
